chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id informed me, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from سماعة, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
If you pray with a group and the Imam recites,
"Recite in the name of your Lord who created,"

or something from the verses of obligatory prostration, and he finishes his recitation and does not prostrate, then indicate by gesture; and the menstruating woman prostrates when she hears the verse of prostration.

key_terms.إِيمَاءً: a gestural indication in place of full physical action
key_terms.السَّجْدَةَ: the prostration triggered by hearing the verse of sajdah
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the prayer leader in congregational salat
key_terms.الْعَزَائِمِ: the Qur'anic passages that require obligatory sajdah
key_terms.فَأَوْمِ: make a gesture or indicate physically

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if the Imam recites a verse of obligatory prostration and does not prostrate, and does a menstruating woman perform the sajdah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning verses of obligatory prostration during congregational salat. It instructs the follower to gesture if the Imam does not perform the prostration, and it states that a menstruating woman should prostrate upon hearing the verse of sajdah.
